- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.8) and understate when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.4), especially in early forecast periods.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment was high and price surged recently.
- Underreact to sustained bullish sentiment; if sentiment remains > 0.7 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast mean by 2–3% to avoid mean reversion lag.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.4–0.8), model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses late-stage mean reversion; if sentiment drops below 0.3 after 15d, reduce forecast slope downward by 1–2% per day.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps > 0.9 and price rises, cap forecast increase to 3–5% max to prevent overcorrection.
